html:
Vuk Stefanović Karadžić was a self taught language reformer, born in 1787 in the village of Tršić in western Serbia, who created the modern Serbian alphabet and literary language.

He served the First Serbian Uprising as a clerk and then lived in Vienna. Following the rule "write as you speak", he made a phonetic version of Cyrillic with one letter for each sound, adding letters such as j and lj. He collected Serbian folk songs and epics, which Goethe and the Grimm brothers admired, and in 1818 published a Serbian dictionary. The church opposed his reforms, but they were adopted in 1868. With Croatian writers he agreed in 1850 on a common standard, the basis of Serbo Croatian.
sum: Vuk Stefanović Karadžić was a self taught language reformer, born in 1787 in the village of Tršić in western Serbia, who created the modern Serbian alphabet and literary language.
